A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. All appendix pages are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original answer-decoding, inflection-point, and early-exit experiments, plus appendix experiments comparing probe baselines, transfer strategies, and hyperparameters.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including decoding comparisons, token-savings measurements, and supplementary probe analyses.

M1.justification: The attention-pooling probes, prefix training, forced answering, CoT monitoring, and confidence-based early exit remain the same. Section 3.2 is shortened and explicitly attributes the probe to prior work; it does not report a changed algorithm or objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU-Redux 2.0 and GPQA-Diamond for the same multiple-choice reasoning and answer-prediction tasks. No dataset, domain, or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain forced answering, the Gemini-2.5-Flash CoT monitor, linear probes, and random-label attention probes. Appendix C and Table 5 are unchanged; the added related-work citations are not new evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Reported model sizes, held-out sample counts, inference settings, training hyperparameters, inflection windows, and early-exit thresholds remain unchanged. The revised token-savings percentages are reporting changes under the same stated settings, not evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the same baseline controls, transfer-versus-fine-tuning comparison, layer and model-size analyses, case-study examples, and inflection threshold/window sweeps. Neither the main-text diagnostic evidence nor the supplementary analyses are expanded or removed.

E5.justification: The inflection-plot error bars and Appendix I conditional counts are unchanged. v4 adds no repeated-run or seed information and makes no change to statistical uncertainty reporting or estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Section 7 changes MMLU token savings at 95% confidence from 80% to 68%, and GPQA savings at 80% confidence from 40% to 50%, retaining the stated 97% performance retention. These revisions better match the unchanged Figure 8; they do not demonstrate new performance gains. Tables, plotted results, and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 removes Section 3.2's explicit mathematical definition of the attention probe, including Equation (1) and the hidden-state and weight-matrix definitions, replacing it with prose and attribution. This formal specification is not relocated to the appendices. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about difficulty-dependent performative reasoning, inflection points, and calibrated early exit. The third contribution is relabeled to emphasize question-level uncertainty, but v1 already distinguished this association from inconsistent temporal correspondence within traces.

C2.justification: The task-difficulty and model-size explanations, qualifications about temporal causality, and cooperative-communication interpretation are retained. The new generic impact statement introduces no substantive applicability boundary or limitation.

D1.justification: The shortened Section 3.2 drops the explicit cross-entropy training-loss statement and parameter specification, reducing self-contained implementation detail. Appendix prompts and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Section 6.3 also standardizes the visualization address to the one already supplied on the first page, without establishing changed resource availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds Afzal et al. (2025) and Ashok and May (2026) to the activation-probing discussion and bibliography. It also explicitly states that the attention probe was introduced by Kantamneni et al. (2025), already cited in v1. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v4 condenses Section 3.2, removes the separate Section 3.5 while retaining the performativity explanation in Section 5, revises the third contribution heading, and makes small case-study and discussion edits. It adds proceedings information and a generic impact statement; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 enlarges the Figure 6 panels, moves Table 2 from page 7 to page 6, and repositions Figure 7 within page 9. Main-text layout also reflows. The same figures and tables are retained, with unchanged underlying graphics and identical appendix layouts.

improvement.justification: The corrected token-savings statements in Section 7 improve agreement with Figure 8, and the added citations and explicit probe attribution improve scholarly clarity. These are limited gains within otherwise unchanged empirical evidence. Removing the probe equation and loss specification reduces methodological self-containment and partly offsets the improvements.
